messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] R Genetic Association Methods and TWAS
messages.subject_clean: R Genetic Association Methods and TWAS
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Develop a more transparent approach to complex genetic data analysis. Advanced Statistical Methods for Genetic Association Studies is a 2-day seminar livestreaming September 8 and 10 with Jingjing Yang (School of Medicine, Emory University). Build R-based workflows for genotype quality control, imputation assessment, and mixed-model genetic association testing. Apply QTL mapping, co-localization, Mendelian Randomization, and TWAS methods with appropriate sensitivity checks. Produce reproducible code and methods descriptions that clarify analytical choices in genetic data research.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/advanced-statistical-methods-for-genetic
Full details are available on the Instats seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] AI-Powered Bioinformatics for Genetic Data
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Integrating genetic measurements across platforms requires careful preparation and validation. AI-Powered Bioinformatics led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Preprocessing, batch correction, imputation, and multi-omics integration provide a basis for analysing heterogeneous genetic datasets. Participants build reproducible Python and R workflows for supervised and unsupervised models, single-cell data, and independent-cohort evaluation. R users working with genetic data can apply these methods to assess cross-modal patterns and interpret model outputs biologically.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/ai-powered-bioinformatics
Further information is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI - livestream seminar
messages.subject_clean: Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI - livestream seminar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone

Instats is excited to offer a 1-day seminar, Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI <https://instats.org/seminar/cell-and-gene-therapy-design-estimands-o>, livestreaming October 6 and sponsored by the American Statistical Association?s Cell and Gene Therapy Scientific Working Group. As cell and gene therapies rapidly reshape biomedical innovation, this seminar provides PhD students, academic researchers, and applied scientists with a coherent framework for evaluating complex interventions across translational research, clinical development, and regulatory evidence generation. Drawing on expertise associated with the American Statistical Association?s Cell and Gene Therapy Scientific Working Group, the workshop examines core design and analysis challenges, including single-arm and randomized trials, dose finding, historical borrowing, estimands, operational considerations, and the production of credible, publishable evidence in settings with limited samples and heterogeneous populations. The seminar also considers the growing role of artificial intelligence in cell and gene therapy development, helping participants understand how emerging computational tools may influence discovery, decision support, evidence synthesis, reproducibility, and interpretation in this fast-moving field.

Sign up today <https://instats.org//seminar/cell-and-gene-therapy-design-estimands-o> to secure your spot, and feel free to share this opportunity with colleagues and students who might benefit!


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
Instats | instats.org

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Tidy Data, Visualisation, and AI
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Reproducible data handling supports careful interpretation of genetic analyses. Tidy Data, Visualisation, and AI is a 2-day seminar livestreaming September 21?22 with Flavio Lombardo (Institute for Statistical and Data Science). Reshape, recode, and check messy data in R using tidyverse tools, then produce adaptable figures with ggplot2. Genetic data analysts can apply these practices to keep data preparation explicit and graphical choices aligned with the scientific question. The seminar includes AI-assisted extraction from unstructured text and methods for validating its results.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/tidy-data-visualisation-and-ai
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Machine Learning for Computational Biology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Genetic datasets often call for methods that extend beyond conventional statistical summaries. Machine Learning for Computational Biology is a seminar livestreaming October 19, led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University). Random forests, neural networks, MCMC, and clustering provide practical approaches to genetic and genomic data analysis in R and Python. Coding algorithms from scratch develops understanding of model construction, gradient descent, feature selection, and optimisation. Researchers can use these methods to investigate complex genetic data and evaluate modelling choices in their own analyses.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/machine-learning-for-computational-biolo-4
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Last seats available — Population Genomics Using Ancient DNA
messages.subject_clean: Last seats available — Population Genomics Using Ancient DNA
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
 
Interested in uncovering population history from ancient DNA?
 
Join us online, 21?25 September, for an hands-on course covering the computational analysis of ancient DNA data, from authentication and variant calling to population structure, demographic inference, allele-sharing statistics, and natural selection.
 
You?ll work with real aDNA datasets and practical research questions, learning methods that can be directly applied to your own research.
 
Designed for graduate students and researchers in genetics, genomics, ecology, anthropology, and population biology.
 
If aDNA and population genomics are part of your research?or you?re looking to add these tools to your toolkit?this is a great opportunity to join us.
 
 
Best,
 
Carlo

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Accessible Bioinformatics for Windows Users
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Genetic analysis can proceed on Windows systems with a suitable computational setup. Accessible Bioinformatics for Windows Users is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 2 and 6, led by Andres Zhou Tsang (Adelaide University). Configure WSL, R, and supporting bioinformatics tools on Windows for genetic data analysis. Process sequencing data, inspect quality, assemble genomes, align sequences, and conduct RNA-seq differential expression analysis. Apply these workflows to genetic datasets while combining Linux-based tools with familiar Windows applications.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/accessible-bioinformatics-for-windows-us
Please circulate this information if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
